Hi Nora — thanks for the heads-up.

On Tue, Jun 7, 2028 at 09:12 Nora Thompson <nora.thompson@garnsley.com> wrote:
> We're stuck on onboarding our supplier (Lumina Parts)...

We see two common failure modes here: (1) Coupa invite redirect originates from an AWS-hosted URL (SES or cloudfront) and some corp firewalls block the token redirect, or (2) SSO assertion is being intercepted by an allowlist that only permits known IdP endpoints.

What I can do immediately:
- Re-provision the vendor from the Redwood admin console so the supplier receives an invite from our admin domain (less likely to trigger redirect blocks).
- Send you the raw invite link (non-wrapped) so your IT can test directly. I've attached the link as coupa_invite_link.txt.
- If whitelisting is needed, ask your IT to allowlist: *.coupa.com and email-sending subdomains from redwood-inference.com and the AWS IP ranges in the attachment.

Ben (CC) handles Coupa admin — Ben, do you want us to create the vendor record and resend once Garnsley confirms firewall changes?

I can also create a one-time access token or temporary vendor record if that speeds things up. Let me know which approach you prefer and I'll act today.

Thanks,
Priyom Das

Nora — thanks for the details. Quick notes from the Coupa side: we commonly see corporate allowlists blocking the initial redirect. If Garnsley's firewall is inspecting or blocking redirects to cloudfront/AWS, the tokenized invite URL will fail before SSO kicks in.

Two practical options:
1) Your IT whitelists the sending IP ranges and the Coupa hostnames (recommended). We can provide an allowlist bundle (IP ranges + hostnames).
2) We can provision 'Lumina Parts' manually in the Coupa tenant with a temporary local account and password; then you can issue the PO immediately and the vendor can update to SSO later.

If you prefer (2), I'll provision and send an admin-created login by end of day. If you prefer (1), please ask your network team to share a short window for us to test.

Also, if your egress NAT is behind a dynamic pool, make sure the NAT public IPs are the ones added — we've seen cases where the allowlist was applied to the wrong CIDR. If your IT team can share a sample firewall log entry (time + dst) we'll correlate it with our invite attempts.

Marissa — looping you in for any procurement-side approvals if we need to create a manual vendor account.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com
